# Yardlet 0.11.11
This release fixes two security issues in 0.11.10. Please update.
## Security
- Filling a saved sign-in now asks you first on more of the pages an agent's script may still reach, including pages that tabs linked to it open or load later. - Each saved connector secret is now tied to the server, mail account, program or account provider it was saved for, and is used only there. Secrets saved before keep working without a new sign-in. - Signing in to a connector's server checks that the sign-in details the server publishes name that same server.
## Tasks
- Turns cut off by a force quit, a crash or a killed process now continue at the next launch, as after a quit. - The task list shows at launch without waiting for every Claude Code title to be read again. - Opening a main window again, from the Dock or with File › New Window, no longer interrupts running tasks. - Launching with a long Codex history no longer keeps Codex busy for half a minute: Yardlet lists Codex threads from Codex's own database, as the Codex app does. - Agent CLIs installed with Homebrew now update automatically. After a CLI updates, idle tasks start the new version with their next message. - Automatic account choices skip accounts whose plan doesn't offer the task's model. - Messages sent while a task waits to switch accounts no longer stay queued behind a background command. - A scheduled run no longer moves its task to another account while the task still has work running. - Schedule changes made in your own task no longer wait on an approval card after the schedule's runs move to new tasks.
## Help
- Help › Report a Problem… opens the bug report form on GitHub with the versions of Yardlet, macOS and your agent CLIs filled in. Error cards and a failed task start offer the same form with the error, after your home folder, names, addresses and token-like text are taken out. Nothing is sent until you submit it on GitHub. - Help › Show Diagnostic Logs opens Yardlet's log folders in the Finder, and Help › Yardlet Help opens the README.
## Interface
- The task header has a Find button. The session rail and terminal buttons have icons of their own, apart from the side panel's. - Tabs at the top of the window, in the side panel and in the window's tab bar, can be dragged instead of moving the window. - The new-task composer has the same + menu as a task's: files, photos, a folder and slash commands. - Removing a connector, or a Google or Microsoft account, asks first, since it signs you out. - Tooltips name their keys, disabled buttons dim, and several small buttons take clicks over a larger area. - A saved sign-in's two-factor code can be removed on its own in the item sheet. - Korean screens no longer show some text in English, and Korean activity lines read correctly.
## Browser
- A tab the agent used before you opened it in the panel takes the panel's size, instead of staying at 1280 by 800 in the panel's corner.
## Another Mac's tasks
- A suggested task's Options works in a window for another Mac. - When the other Mac doesn't do what the window asked, the window says why, and shows the task's error card and composer notices as the Mac does.
## Faster
- A long conversation takes less of the app's time for each streamed update, and a Codex answer wakes the app less often. - Searching the sidebar no longer redraws the window for every streamed update. - A streaming task saves only what changed in its reading copy, instead of rewriting the whole conversation every second. - Saving schedules no longer holds up the window while the disk is busy. - An account check no longer keeps a CPU core busy after the CLI exits.
## Fixes
- The Agents card no longer lists a retried `run_agent` call twice. - Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 sessions show their cost.

# Yardlet 0.11.10
## Signing in on a first run
- If you use Claude Code through the Claude app, your history comes over but the CLI has no sign-in of its own, because the app keeps its sign-in to itself. Yardlet used to look connected and let the first turn fail with `/login`. Now the login reads "Not signed in" on its row and on the new-task screen, which offers Sign in before you write anything. - A new task on a signed-out login stays on the new-task screen with your draft and Sign in, instead of becoming a failed task. This works for Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity CLI. - A task already on a signed-out login stops at once with a Sign in button, instead of after up to 30 seconds of waiting. When another signed-in account shares the task's history, the card also offers to continue with that account. - A sign-in works right away, with no restart: new tasks start on the account you signed in with, and a task that found no login resumes the same conversation with your next message. This includes a sign-in that finishes while Yardlet is still reading the login for the first time. - A Codex task on a signed-out login stops at its turn and offers Sign in, instead of retrying and ending in an error. A Codex setup with a model provider of your own no longer reads as signed out. - The account chip no longer shows an address from a config file as the account while the CLI can't confirm it. - Yardlet finds Claude Code from your login shell's PATH, including installs through asdf, mise and `~/.claude/local`, when it was opened from the Dock or Finder. - Checking your limits no longer stops Claude Code while it may be renewing its login, which could sign it out. - Sign-in checks are recorded on this Mac in `~/.yardlet/logs/account-checks.log`, without credentials, addresses or CLI output. If Claude Code still doesn't start for you, attaching that file to a [bug report](https://github.com/zzunkie/yardlet/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml) helps.
## Tasks
- A split view no longer repeats its tasks in the title bar: each pane heads its own task. With one tab, the panes reach the window's top, and the empty part of a top pane's header moves the window. The Split View menu and the command palette now offer Rename, Pin and Archive beside End split view. - A Claude Code task can keep a context limit of its own, so one long task compacts earlier while the others keep Claude Code's default. Choose it from Context limit in the composer's context ring. An idle task applies it at once, and a busy one when its turn ends. Child tasks, forks and side chats start without it. - A Cloud section after the tasks lists your Codex Cloud tasks, which open in your browser, and the Codex tasks your dots started, which open in Personal agents. Claude Code cloud sessions and Codex's newer cloud threads aren't listed, since neither agent offers a way to list them.
## Connectors
- A service with several accounts (Google's, Microsoft's and Mail) now offers each tool once, with a required `account` argument, instead of a full copy of its tools for every account. With six Google accounts that was 234 tools. - A call naming no account, or one Yardlet doesn't have, is refused before anything is sent, and one naming an account turned off in the task is refused as off. Approval cards and conversation rows name the account a call uses. - A call refused for a missing argument now lists the values it takes, such as the accounts to choose from. - Connector tools with long names now reach Antigravity CLI, which dropped three Notion tools before. - Mail's search for IMAP accounts searches only the folder it's given. - Claude Code tasks continued from before this update may say once that Yardlet's tools disconnected, or have a connector call refused until it names `account`. The tools still work.
## Antigravity and other ACP agents
- Turns that quitting or updating Yardlet cut off now continue at the next launch, as Claude Code and Codex turns do. This covers Antigravity, OpenCode, Kimi Code, Grok Build and Hermes. - Turns Antigravity starts on its own, when a subagent or a background task ends, now show as they run, with the usual unread mark and notification. Stop cancels them. Before, they sat unseen until your next message. - Yardlet removes the schema folders Antigravity CLI leaves behind for each task, about 2 MB each. Folders a running process may still read stay. - One spent group of models no longer reads as out for every model: with Antigravity's Gemini group nearly out, a task on another model keeps its room. - The new-task model menu lists Antigravity's models before any task has run, and says when it couldn't read them.
## Accounts and limits
- When every account of a harness is nearly out, `list_accounts`, `create_task` and `run_agent` tell the agent which other harnesses have room. Which harness a task uses stays the agent's choice, and this adds no check or model turn.
## Another Mac's tasks
- A window for another Mac stays connected through the relay. A long answer could close the connection, which the direct paths hid. - A window for another Mac also tries the relay's second address, which is nearer on many networks. - A window closed right after it opened keeps what it showed for the next time. - The browser panel lays the page out at the panel's size, instead of drawing a 1280 by 800 picture at its width with empty room below. - A tab handed over behind another task keeps its size, so the panel and the agent's screenshots get the page instead of a square of one color, often black. - The panel lists a task's browser tabs as the task opens, and says when a tab shows only on the host. - A file page the task's agent opened in a tab shows there too. Other files outside the task's folders stay on the host. - Pictures an agent generated, with Antigravity's `generate_image` or Codex's image generation, count as the task's outputs: they open from the file link and show on the Outputs card. - Small trackpad scrolls no longer end in "The page didn't take that". - The title bar row starts at the window's top, as in a local window.
## Security
- Remote connections are hardened: what they accept from a relay, a paired device or a pairing request is held to stricter limits.
## Browser
- Typing Korean, Japanese or Chinese in a page keeps your text when you click another field, the address field or the composer, as in Chrome. - A `browser_screenshot` that waits asks the tab for a frame. When it still gets no picture, it says the tab drew none, and how to recover. - One-time code fields named a verification PIN, such as LinkedIn's, take a filled code.
## Faster
- Saving drafts, split views, account readings and address history no longer holds up the app while the disk is busy. - The session rail no longer asks the disk on every draw.
## Fixes
- If Yardlet can't open its task list at launch, it says so in the window for the whole run and leaves your saved window layout, projects, schedules and drafts as they were, instead of saving an empty layout over them. - An archived task no longer sends a usage-limit continue later. - ACP tool lines no longer read "read Reading README.md". - The terminal reports a shell's real exit status under load, where it sometimes said 0. - An agent's API settings no longer reach an app it opens.
## Thanks
Thanks to @rupamkgp for the work on showing cloud sessions in the task list (#226), which the Cloud section came from.

# Yardlet 0.11.9
## Intel Macs
- Yardlet now has a version for Intel Macs with macOS 15 or later: `Yardlet-0.11.9-x86_64.dmg`, or `brew install --cask zzunkie/tap/yardlet`, which picks it on an Intel Mac. It updates itself from a feed of its own. - This is the first Intel version. It has been tried on one Intel Mac, a 2018 Mac mini with Intel UHD Graphics 630 on macOS 15.8, where it starts, streams a task and draws the built-in browser. Other Intel graphics (Iris, AMD Radeon) and macOS 26 on Intel have not been tried yet. - Its built-in browser plays no H.264 video or AAC audio, such as many sites' MP4 videos; WebM video (VP9, AV1) plays. - If you use it, please tell us how it goes, especially if the built-in browser closes or stays blank: a [bug report](https://github.com/zzunkie/yardlet/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml) with "Intel" chosen, or a note in [Discussions](https://github.com/zzunkie/yardlet/discussions).
## Accounts and limits
- New tasks start on Automatic when a harness has more than one account in automatic assignment, and the composer names the account it picks and why. An account you choose stays until you choose Automatic again. - A Claude Code task stopped by a usage limit that resets within a day continues by itself at the reset, as Claude Code does, and messages other tasks send it meanwhile wait until then. Settings › Harness Accounts › Continue automatically at usage limit turns this off. - Claude Code tasks move to an account with room when it costs nothing: an idle task on a nearly spent account moves once its prompt cache has expired, and a task a limit stopped continues on an account with room. Settings › Harness Accounts › Move tasks to an account with room turns this off. - Settings › Usage shows the tokens Claude Code and Codex record on this Mac, with their API-equivalent cost, beside the plan limits, and Home shows today's tokens and the limits closest to running out. The counts stay on this Mac; Settings › Usage › Count token usage turns this off and deletes them. - A limit card read back after a relaunch offers Resume again. - Each row in Settings › Harness Accounts has a "…" menu, with Sign Out… and Sign In With Another Account… for the default login.
## Tasks
- Group the task list by state (Needs input, Working, Unread, Idle) from the menu beside its search field. - Archived tasks open read-only without being unarchived. - Rename from Recent Conversation, beside Rename, has Claude Code or Codex name a long task again from its latest turns. - Move to Chats takes any task out of its project. - Codex tasks offer the Codex app's permissions: Ask for approval, Approve for me and Full access, and Custom when config.toml sets its own. You can choose one on the new-task screen, and schedules start with theirs. - Ask an agent in the conversation to change a Yardlet setting. A change that lowers a protection asks you on the approval card first. - Settings groups its sections under Personal, Integrations and Harnesses, and Accounts is now Harness Accounts.
## Terminal
- Settings › General › Terminal location opens the terminal below the conversation or as a tab in the side panel, as in the Codex app. Split Terminal in its header shows two shells side by side. - Shell code blocks in answers offer Run in terminal beside Copy code, and Run in terminal on a command card now runs the command instead of only typing it.
## Browser, files and mail
- Tasks share the built-in browser's sign-ins, so a site you sign in to is signed in for every task. A task gets a browser profile of its own only when its agent signs in to a site itself. Task profiles from earlier versions are merged once, and the emptied ones go to the Trash. - Agents try the password manager before handing a sign-in to you, and ask you before keeping a two-factor setup they started. - The blocked pop-up menu can always allow pop-ups from a site, so its sign-in or payment window opens as the site meant. - An agent can dismiss a site's permission request in its own task's tabs; only you can allow one. - Files previews movies, audio and animated images. - Agents can attach files to Outlook and IMAP drafts, as to Gmail drafts. - IMAP accounts on servers such as Naver Mail now get new-mail notices and search results.
## Privacy
- Screenshots an agent takes in the built-in browser hide keys and tokens, as its text results already did. - Links you open from mail open in the mailbox's own browser panel, out of reach of task agents.
## Faster
- Long conversations stream with much less work on the main thread, so the task list scrolls smoothly while a Codex answer streams, and scrolling up draws earlier turns one at a time. - Resizing a window with a long conversation, opening Personal agents and saving connector settings no longer hold up the app. - The Mac connects to the phone relay faster on many networks.
## Fixes
- Agents start with your login shell's PATH, so tools such as Homebrew's `gh` are found when Yardlet was opened from the Dock or Finder. - The Settings card in the session rail stays inside the side panel with a long model name. - Clicking a link in an answer that is still streaming no longer freezes Yardlet. - After a crash, Yardlet ends the Claude Code processes it left running instead of reporting their tasks as open in another app. - An ACP agent whose process ended on its own starts again for the next prompt. - A Codex turn cut off by a lost connection continues once the network is back. - A subagent asked to run on a model its harness does not offer stops with an error instead of using the default model. - Dragging a task row in the sidebar now works, to nest it under another task or drop it onto a split view. - A link followed directly by Korean, Japanese or Chinese text no longer takes in the text. - A chat without a title from its harness no longer shows its folder name.
## Thanks
Thanks to @minsujang0 for reporting the slow scrolling while Codex streams (#183), the Settings card overflow (#483) and the missing PATH (#485), and for suggesting grouping tasks by state (#489).
